item.title: Congress Targets Deepfakes and Arbitration in New Child‑Safety Bills
item.description:
Congress Targets Deepfakes and Arbitration in New Child‑Safety Bills

Lawmakers are moving to give victims of online harm new legal tools before the end of 2026, focusing on deepfake creators, forced arbitration, and platforms like Roblox.

🔍 Overview

  • Lawmakers are trying to pass new protections for victims of online harm before the end of 2026, targeting deepfake creators and online platforms that block users from filing lawsuits.
  • Congress is scrambling to provide legal recourse for deepfakes and online grooming.
  • The session ends in a little more than three weeks.

📜 Legislative Actions

  • Senate Judiciary Subcommittee Hearing – Called for ending forced arbitration for online harms, targeting Roblox for using arbitration clauses on minors.
  • Hawley‑Durbin Bill – Would render arbitration agreements unenforceable for disputes over alleged child sexual exploitation or “child cyber injury.”
  • Blumenthal‑Britt‑Booker Bill – Similar approach, explicitly covering data‑privacy violations.
  • Defiance Act – Sponsored by Reps. Alexandria Ocasio‑Cortez and Laurel Lee; would let victims of non‑consensual intimate deepfakes sue creators for damages.

🏢 Targeted Companies

  • Roblox – Facing about 180 lawsuits in a consolidated case over its alleged role in failing to protect children. The platform enforces forced arbitration clauses even for users as young as 10.
  • Tech companies and perpetrators – Could become vulnerable to a new wave of legal challenges if the bills pass.

🗣️ Voices & Quotes

  • “The best thing we can do in terms of enforcement is we can open up the courthouse doors,” Sen. Josh Hawley (R‑MO) told reporters after the Roblox hearing.
  • Hawley called the jury system “corruption‑proof” and “an incredibly big hammer.”
  • “Safety has been central to Roblox since we launched. We require age checks for chat, place users under 16 in age‑based accounts with protective defaults, and block images and video in chat,” said Roblox’s global head of public policy Nicky Jackson Colaço.
  • Paris Hilton: “Some people might have thought that was the end of my fight. But when I make a promise to survivors, I keep it.”
  • Hilton noted that over 50 million people have been victimized by sexually explicit deepfakes and that “strangers have created over 100,000 AI‑generated explicit images and videos portraying me.”
  • Law professor Myriam Gilles: passing either proposal “would have a profound impact.”

📊 Bills at a Glance

Bill Sponsors Primary Aim
Hawley‑Durbin Arbitration Bill Sen. Josh Hawley (R‑MO), Sen. Dick Durbin (D‑IL) Make arbitration agreements unenforceable for child sexual exploitation/​cyber injury disputes
Blumenthal‑Britt‑Booker Bill Sens. Richard Blumenthal (D‑CT), Katie Britt (R‑AL), Cory Booker (D‑NJ) End forced arbitration; explicitly cover data‑privacy violations
Defiance Act Reps. Alexandria Ocasio‑Cortez (D‑NY), Laurel Lee (R‑FL) Allow victims of non‑consensual intimate deepfakes to sue creators

⚖️ Why It Matters

  • Litigation has become one of the more successful ways for survivors of online harm to seek change.
  • Ending forced arbitration could expose platform practices to public discovery, something currently hidden under arbitration.
  • If the Defiance Act or arbitration bans pass, creators of harmful deepfakes and platforms that enable them could face increased legal and financial liability.
  • The push reflects broader congressional frustration with missed deadlines on child‑safety, privacy, and consumer‑protection bills, even as the Take It Down Act begins to address deepfakes.

#deepfakes #legislation #childsafety #arbitration

Source: Tech lawsuits defined 2026 — and lawmakers want more

item.title: US House to Vote on Bipartisan Bill Protecting Households from Data Center Power Costs
item.description:
US House to Vote on Bipartisan Bill Protecting Households from Data Center Power Costs

The US House of Representatives is expected to vote on the bipartisan ‘Ratepayer Protection Act’ this Wednesday. The legislation aims to prevent the soaring costs associated with data center expansion and power needs from being passed on to average household electricity bills.

🔍 Overview

Introduced by Representative Kathy Castor (D-FL) and Representative Gabe Evans (R-CO), the bill seeks to ensure that large data centers pay their fair share of the costs for expanding the electricity grid. The proposal comes as government officials face pressure to manage the increasing energy demands of the AI industry while protecting consumer affordability and grid reliability.

🧩 How it works

  • Cost Allocation: State utility regulators would be required to consider whether large electricity users should pay for the infrastructure needed to serve them.
  • Capacity Threshold: The proposed rules would require new data centers using at least 20 megawatts to cover the additional power infrastructure costs they create.
  • Rate Reductions: Regulators would have the authority to charge large data centers extra to help lower the bills of other utility customers.
  • State Authority: The bill would give states more freedom to impose conditions, such as requiring data centers to secure new power supplies or placing limits on their electricity usage.

⚙️ Key details

The following reactions and perspectives have been reported regarding the proposed legislation:

Entity or Individual Position Perspective
Hakeem Jeffries House Democratic Leader Called the proposal an ‘appropriate step forward’ but noted ‘more clearly needs to be done.’
Allison Clements Former FERC member Described the bill as a ‘modest step in the right direction’ that signals congressional alignment on protecting customers.
Craig Sundstrom Amazon Energy Policy Director Stated the bill ‘could unlock the investment needed to build new generation and transmission faster.’
Ari Peskoe Harvard Electricity Law Initiative Highlighted that no other industry’s electricity usage has captured so much political attention.
Technology Industry Official (Via Axios) Described certain provisions as an ‘unprecedented level of discriminatory treatment’ for a single industry.

💡 Why it matters

While data centers have existed for decades, the growth of AI has significantly increased the demand for new power plants and grid upgrades. This shift has raised concerns regarding higher costs for households. The bipartisan support for the bill arrives ahead of the November midterm elections, highlighting the political priority of grid reliability and consumer costs. While Amazon suggests the bill could accelerate infrastructure investment, the Data Center Coalition is currently reviewing the legislation. Microsoft, Google, and Nvidia declined to comment, while Meta did not respond to requests for comment.

#DataCenters #EnergyPolicy #ArtificialIntelligence #Legislation

Source: US moves to stop AI data centres from pushing up household electricity bills. Here’s what could change for Americans
